roles.keeper: You are <ALIAS>, the KEEPER of the lighthouse. You see the whole maze and you cannot move. Three blind runners are in it. Your words are the only bridge from what you can see to what they can do, and every transmission costs an extra tick of tide.
roles.runner: You are <ALIAS>, a blind RUNNER in a flooding maze. You see only the three-by-three window around yourself. The keeper sees everything and can talk to you, but only one message per tick and it always arrives a tick late.

briefings.canonical:
Rules:
- The maze is a perfect maze: exactly one path between any two floor
  tiles, no loops. The only gap in the outer wall is the EXIT on the top
  row.
- Three KEYS lie in the maze. When all of them have been picked up the
  gate at the exit opens (a horn everyone hears) and runners standing on
  the exit tile escape.
- The TIDE rises from the bottom row upward and never recedes. It is a
  function of one number, the CLOCK. Every tick the clock advances by 1,
  and by 2 instead if the keeper transmitted that tick. Nobody may step
  into water; a runner the water reaches drowns.
- SCORE is a single team number shared by all four seats: 6 points for
  the keys, 10 for every runner that escapes, and up to 6 more for
  escaping with all three while the clock is still low. Higher is better.
  Drowning simply earns nothing.
- The keeper may transmit ONE short message per tick. It reaches all
  three runners at the start of the NEXT tick. Runners have no channel at
  all: not to the keeper, not to each other.
- Your notes are private to you and fed back to you every tick.
briefings.plain:
The perfect maze has exactly one route between any two floor tiles and no loops. Its only opening through the outer wall is the EXIT in the top row. Collect all three keys to open the exit gate; everyone hears the horn. A runner on the open exit escapes.

Water rises from the bottom row and never retreats. The CLOCK determines the tide. A silent tick advances the clock by one; a tick with a keeper transmission advances it by two. Water is impassable, and a runner reached by it drowns.

All four seats share one team score: six points for the keys, ten per escaped runner, and up to six extra when all three escape with clock time remaining. Higher is better; drowning earns no points.

The keeper can send at most one short message per tick to all three runners. It arrives at the start of the next tick. Runners cannot send messages to the keeper or each other. Your notes remain private and are returned every tick.
